jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Executive Director is **monca’s** chief staff leader and is responsible for fundraising, organizational leadership, community engagement, and day\-to\-day administration. This is a hands\-on position: the successful candidate will set direction while also following through on the practical work required in a small nonprofit. The Executive Director will work closely with the Board while maintaining clear responsibility for staff leadership and routine operations.

**Position:** Full\-time, approximately 40 hours per week  
**Compensation:** $70,000–$80,000 in annual base compensation, or $33\.65–$38\.46 per hour under an hourly structure, depending on experience and final position structure  
**Reports to:** Board of Directors

**Application deadline:** Open until filled; priority consideration by September 19, 2026\. ***Position open until filled.***

**Primary responsibilities**

* Lead contributed\-revenue efforts, including individual giving, grants, sponsorships, donor cultivation, timely charitable\-contribution acknowledgment letters, donor\-wall updates, and other year\-round donor recognition and stewardship.
* Develop a practical annual fundraising plan with measurable goals, timelines, and shared responsibilities for the ED and Board.
* Supervise, support, and coordinate staff; establish priorities, clarify roles, and foster a respectful, accountable workplace.
* Manage museum operations, programs, contracts, policies, legal and regulatory compliance, and other day\-to\-day administrative needs.
* Oversee museum\-store operations, including purchasing, inventory, merchandising, organization, and related systems.
* Coordinate building maintenance and repairs with Butte County and outside service providers, including HVAC, plumbing, and other facility needs.
* Recruit, orient, train, support, and coordinate museum volunteers.
* Serve as liaison between the Exhibition and Collections Committees, museum staff, and the Board. The Exhibition Committee leads artist selection and curatorial planning; the ED coordinates schedules, budgets, contracts, staffing, promotion, installation, visitor experience, and communication with the Board.
* Work with the Treasurer and bookkeeper to prepare the annual budget, monitor results, manage cash needs, and provide clear financial information to the Board.
* Serve as a visible and constructive representative of monca with artists, donors, members, volunteers, public agencies, community organizations, and the media.
* Support the Board with timely reports, well\-framed decisions, and reliable follow through, while maintaining appropriate separation between governance and operations.
* Advance monca’s mission and strategic priorities, including thoughtful evaluation of future facility and program needs.

**Qualifications**

* Demonstrated leadership in a nonprofit, museum, arts organization, educational institution, public agency, or similarly mission\-driven setting.
* A credible record of fundraising or closely related work involving donors, grants, sponsorships, partnerships, or revenue development.
* Strong relationship\-building and conflict\-management skills, with a leadership style grounded in respect, clarity, listening, sound boundaries, and accountability.
* Ability to manage competing priorities and complete both strategic and administrative work in a small organization.
* Sound financial understanding, including budgeting and interpreting financial reports.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Strong practical digital skills, including the ability to collaborate with off\-site board members, volunteers, contractors, and other team members through shared documents, cloud drives, calendars, video meetings, and related online tools.
* Ability to learn and use point\-of\-sale, donor\-management, and other operating systems. Experience with Shopify, Bloomerang, and comparable platforms is especially welcome.
* Commitment to Northern California art and to welcoming, community\-focused cultural institutions. A background
* as a practicing artist or curator is welcome but not required.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Museum experience is welcome but not required.
* Position structure and benefits
* **monca**

expects this to be a full\-time, primarily on\-site position in Chico, averaging approximately 40 hours per week, with occasional evening and weekend responsibilities and reasonable flexibility in scheduling. Because strong candidates may have limited outside professional commitments, **monca** will determine the most appropriate structure  
with the selected candidate. The position may be offered as hourly/nonexempt or salaried. Any exempt classification and salary will comply with California law. All monca work must be accurately accounted for under the final arrangement.

**monca** is evaluating health\-benefit options. Depending on eligibility, participation requirements, and the plan adopted by **monca**, the successful candidate may be offered access to group health coverage or another lawful health\-benefit arrangement with a modest employer contribution. The exact compensation and benefit terms will be stated clearly before an offer is accepted. Benefits are not convertible to cash unless expressly permitted by the applicable plan and law.  
Reasonable, disclosed outside professional activity may be permitted when it does not conflict with monca’s interests, interfere with the agreed schedule or performance expectations, or prevent the ED from serving as monca’s primary staff leader.

How to apply

Please send a résumé and a cover letter describing your interest in monca, relevant leadership experience, and experience building contributed revenue to **heather@monca.org**. Applications will be reviewed as received. Finalists should be prepared to discuss their approach to the first year of fundraising, staff leadership, and community relationship\-building.

**Position Description**

 **Position:** Director of Communications

**Employer:** Vitamin Angels

**Department:** Marketing \& Communications

**Location:** U.S. Remote

**Salary Range:** $130,000\-170,000

***Every applicant is required to submit a cover letter with their application.***

 **About Vitamin Angels**


Vitamin Angels is a global health organization working to save lives and improve the health of women and children most at risk through proven nutrition solutions. We prioritize high\-impact, cost\-effective, evidence\-based nutrition interventions and apply evidence, implementation learning, and innovation to introduce, strengthen, and scale nutrition programs in geographies where we can achieve the greatest and most sustainable impact. Our programs are advanced through long\-term partnerships that enable government and local partner ownership, are implemented within existing structures, and adapted to local contexts.


Vitamin Angels is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a supportive environment where all individuals have access to equal opportunities to succeed, regardless of background, identity, or perspective. Our efforts aim to ensure fairness and mutual respect for all employees, promoting a culture of belonging and professional growth.

**Role or Purpose of Position**


The Director of Communications is responsible for advancing Vitamin Angels’ visibility, credibility, reputation, and influence through strategic external and internal communications. The Director of Communications translates Vitamin Angels’ enterprise narrative into compelling communications that engage audiences, strengthen relationships, elevate organizational expertise, enhance credibility, position Vitamin Angels as a leading global health organization amongst diverse priority audiences, and build understanding and alignment across the organization.


As a senior communications leader, this role oversees corporate communications, media relations, executive communications, thought leadership, external editorial strategy, reputation management, crisis communications, and internal communications. The Director of Communications works closely with the VP of Marketing \& Communications, various functional unit leads within Marketing and Communications, and technical and area experts throughout the organization to build Vitamin Angels recognition as a recognized industry thought leader and credible global health organization\-of\-choice.


The Director of Communications also partners closely with CEO, senior leadership team, People and Culture, and cross\-functional teams to develop and deliver an effective internal communications strategy to unite the organization around common goals, systems, and strategies.

**Major Duties and Responsibilities**


External Communications \& Reputation

Thought Leadership

* Serve as a strategic and trusted communications advisor to the VP Marketing \& Communications, CEO, senior leadership team, and other organizational leaders, advising on messaging, positioning, and reputational opportunities/challenges.
* Partner with key stakeholders from across the organization, including local country team members, to identify communications opportunities and translate organizational priorities into effective communications strategies.
* Identify and train spokespeople and find/create opportunities for Vitamin Angels’ leaders and technical experts to contribute to important conversations through media, speaking engagements, opinion pieces, panels, conferences, podcasts, and other influential platforms.
* Create a culture of thought leadership where key stakeholders (senior leadership team, technical experts, Board directors, etc.) understand the importance and value of looking for thought leadership opportunities and/or acting as thought leaders on behalf of Vitamin Angels.

**DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT AND MAJOR GIFTS**

 **Status**: FT Exempt

**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer

**Schedule of Hours:** Monday – Friday, 9\-5 with occasional evenings and weekends

**Possible Percentage of Work from Home:** 50% or more onsite

**Mandated Reporter:** No

 **ABOUT CORA**


CORA (Community Overcoming Relationship Abuse) is the only agency in San Mateo County solely focused on serving people experiencing intimate partner abuse. CORA provides comprehensive services including a 24\-hour hotline, emergency shelter, legal services, counseling, community education, and prevention programming. CORA is a multicultural agency committed to serving individuals regardless of age, ethnicity, race, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, immigration status, religion, financial status, language, or mental or physical ability.

**THE POSITION**


The Director of Development and Major Gifts leads CORA’s development department and is responsible for achieving an annual fundraising goal of approximately $3 million. The Director sets departmental priorities, establishes measurable goals, manages and develops staff, and uses fundraising data to evaluate performance and guide strategy.


This is a high\-touch fundraising leadership role with significant personal responsibility for major donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Director manages a portfolio of approximately 140 major gift prospects and donors, builds the major donor pipeline, develops corporate and community partnerships, and leads strategies to increase donor acquisition, retention, and upgrades, including planned giving.


The Director works closely with the CEO, Board members, Board Development Committee, CFO, and development and marketing teams to strengthen CORA’s fundraising capacity and long\-term financial sustainability.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead, supervise, coach, and develop a team of three development staff who oversee foundations portfolio, special events, individual giving and marketing and communications.
* Establish departmental goals, priorities, work plans, and performance expectations.
* Monitor results, use data to identify gaps and opportunities, and hold staff accountable for measurable goals.
* Oversee the development budget and department systems, including donor management and tracking platforms.
* Partner with the CEO/CFO on vendors, consultants, and technology that strengthen development capacity.
**Major Gifts**

* Manage and grow a portfolio of approximately 140 major gift prospects and donors through face\-to\-face and virtual meetings, calls, solicitations, and personalized stewardship.
* Build and manage a strong major donor pipeline through prospect identification, research, qualification, cultivation, and solicitation.
* Develop strategies to increase donor acquisition, retention, and upgrades.
* Strengthen long\-term relationships with major donors and provide meaningful opportunities for engagement.
**Corporate \& Community Partnerships**

* Develop and implement strategies for corporate giving and sponsorships.
* Identify and cultivate businesses, corporate leaders, and community partners whose interests align with CORA’s mission.
* Personally cultivate and steward high\-value relationships and participate in solicitations.
**Development Strategy \& Campaigns**

* Develop and execute an integrated annual strategic plan across major gifts, individual giving, foundations, corporations, sponsorships, community partnerships, events, and campaigns.
* Use donor data, analytics, pipeline information, and campaign results to evaluate performance and refine strategy.
* Establish and monitor key development metrics and benchmarks.
* Create new initiatives to increase donor acquisition, retention, repeat giving, and overall fundraising capacity.
* Plan and oversee annual and special campaigns, for example, End of Year and Giving Tuesday.
**Special Events**

* Oversee fundraising events with revenue, donor acquisition, cultivation, and stewardship goals.
* Develop donor\-focused and VIP opportunities in collaboration with the development team.
* Evaluate event results and incorporate lessons learned into future strategy.
**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Minimum of 5–7 years of progressive experience in fundraising, donor cultivation, major gifts, nonprofit development, or a related field.

**Community Missions Corporation \- St. Joseph, MO**

Founded in 2004 as a nonprofit, 501(c)(3\) organization, Community Missions Corporation strives to eliminate chronic homelessness in Northwest Missouri. CMC provides permanent housing for chronically homeless individuals in St. Joseph and Buchanan County Missouri. We believe in the power of community. Our programs are designed to uplift individuals and families, providing necessary resources and support.

**Programs Operating Today**

**Haven House:** St. Joseph's Haven opened its doors on September 9, 2009, to an eagerly awaiting throng of men. St. Joseph's Haven houses 18 chronically homeless men in 9 semi\-private suites. “The Haven” also incorporates a "Safe Haven" component into its repertoire of services, providing shelter for up to 7 additional men during crisis situations.

**Juda House:** Juda House provides housing to sixteen (16\) chronically homeless men who are diagnosed with one or more disabilities. Case managers at Community Missions work to assure that the basic needs of each man in our care are met so that he can then begin addressing those issues that have rendered him homeless time and time again\- things like serious mental illness, alcohol and drug addiction, physical impairment.

**24 Hour Emergency Shelter \- My Brother's House:** Community Missions’ 24\-Hour Shelter provides a safe, supportive environment for both men and women experiencing homelessness in St. Joseph and the surrounding area. Unlike traditional shelters with limited hours, our facility is open around the clock, ensuring guests have consistent access to shelter, meals, restrooms, and basic needs every day of the year.

**Executive Director \- Job Description**

The Executive Director serves as the Chief Operations Officer of Community Missions Corporation and is responsible for the overall leadership, supervision, daily operations, strategic planning, program oversight, and organizational compliance. The Executive Director ensures the organization's mission is fulfilled by providing strong operational leadership, maintaining quality services, supporting staff development, and fostering community partnerships.

Because Community Missions Corp. programs operate 24/7, the Executive Director is expected to ensure that the needs of our programs are being met continuously. This may require attention to staff and programming outside of typical business hours.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* The Executive Director reports directly to the Board of Directors.
* Oversee progress, growth, and operations of CMC programs and initiatives.
* Develop and maintain a strong knowledge of issues surrounding homelessness, related services and community resources.
* Ensure safety of all staff and program participants.
* Maintain partnership with the Board of Directors and community stakeholders to address current needs and trends related to homelessness.
* Perform administrative and financial duties necessary to support the continued operation and growth of CMC.
* Seek, secure, and manage funding sources, including but not limited to grants.
* Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Maintain document control and policy updates.
* Attend community meetings and build collaborative relationships with outside entities as an ambassador for Community Missions.
* Direct supervision of all program staff, Shelter Leads, Care Coordinators, Outreach staff, Case Managers, Peer Support staff, volunteers, and interns.
* All other duties as deemed necessary. These inclusions are descriptive, not exhaustive.

**Knowledge, Skills \& Abilities**

* Collaborative leadership approach within the organization and community.
* Conflict resolution and crisis intervention.
* Strong decision\-making and problem\-solving skills.

**Qualifications \& Requirements**

* Full\-time, salaried position.
* Duties performed on\-site and off\-site.
* Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
* Bachelor's degree required in a related competency; Master's degree preferred.

**About the Indiana Department of Workforce Development (DWD):**
  

Our mission is to develop a premier workforce that will allow Indiana employers to flourish and entice businesses from outside our state to relocate to Indiana. Everyone at DWD will be required to think outside\-the\-box; to determine metrics that will allow for measurement and improvement and efficiencies to be made along the way. If managed properly, Indiana’s workforce will be second to none and completely prepared for the next phase of the state and country’s economic growth.

  

**Role Overview:**


The Indiana Commission of Service \& Volunteerism (Serve Indiana) is housed within the Indiana Department of Workforce Development. Serve Indiana mobilizes people and resources to deliver creative solutions to community problems. The Executive Director is responsible for overseeing all agency division functions; leadership of a team to carry out Serve Indiana's strategic objectives set by the Governor\-appointed Commission, AmeriCorps programs, and the agency; as well as all grants, reports, and the division's budget. Serve Indiana is part of the Business and Community Engagement team and the Executive Director plays a leadership role in cross\-functional work within the team. The short version

We run a DTC e\-commerce brand scaled primarily through paid social. The team is remote: creative strategists, video editors, two media buyers, customer service, plus a stack of outside agencies.

We're hiring a COO to be the quality assurance backbone of the business. Every function has a standard. Your job is to know what that standard is, check that it's being met, and catch problems before they cost us revenue — an editor shipping ads nobody would click, a supplier quietly slipping two weeks past the ship date, an agency billing us monthly for work that isn't moving a number, a customer email sitting unanswered for three days.

Nobody is doing that job right now. The founder is, badly, in between everything else. That's the gap.

You'll also become the front door for the business. Team leads report to you — the editing pod leads, customer service — and agencies come to you first. You run those meetings, make the call, and loop the founder in when something is big enough to need it.

Read this part before you apply

This business runs on urgency. The founder's single biggest operational strength is responding and following up fast enough that nothing sits — every moving part gets delivered on time because somebody is on it within minutes, not at the end of the day.

That standard transfers to you. If a message needs a response with urgency and you don't give it one, you will be fired. Not warned twice, not coached through it. This isn't about being glued to your phone 24/7 or replying to everything instantly — it's about judgment: knowing which messages can wait until tomorrow and which ones stop a shipment, a launch, or a spend decision if they sit for six hours. Getting that wrong repeatedly is the fastest way out of this role.

If that reads as harsh, this isn't the job for you. If it reads as obvious, keep going.

What you'll oversee

Listed in order of importance to the business.

1\. Video editing team

Our creative volume drives our revenue. This is the sector where your attention pays off most. You're responsible for making sure editors hit their KPIs — concepts shipped, turnaround time, revisions cleared, overdue work — and that what they ship is actually good, not just delivered on time. You'll need to connect creative output to ad account performance and be able to say which editors are producing winners and which are producing filler.

2\. Creative strategists

Scripts need to show real strategic thinking: a specific angle, a real customer objection, a reason this hook works for this product. What we don't want is a script pasted out of an AI tool with no judgment applied. You'll read the work, push back when it's thin, and hold the bar. This requires you to actually understand direct response — you can't spot lazy strategy if you don't know what good strategy looks like.

3\. Supply chain

Our supplier commits to shipping times and successful deliveries. You make sure they hit them. That means tracking POs against promised dates, flagging slippage early, staying on top of inventory levels before we stock out, and having the conversation with the supplier when they miss. A stockout costs us more in a week than most other problems on this list cost us in a month.

4\. Agency management

We work with agencies across Google, CRO, retention/email, SMS, post\-purchase flows, accounting, TikTok Shop, and development. You own all of these relationships and you're the main point of contact for every one of them. You run the calls, set the agenda, and hold them to what they committed to. The founder joins when something is high\-stakes enough to warrant it, but the default is that you handle it and report back.

For each agency: what did they promise, what are they delivering, what is it costing us, and is it worth it? You'll cut the ones that are coasting.

5\. Team time and accountability

We run Hubstaff across the team. You review it — who's actually working the hours they're billing, and whether those hours are going toward the work that matters. The number you care about is hours against output, not raw activity. Someone logging 40 hours with nothing to show for it is a bigger problem than someone logging 30 and shipping everything on time, and you should be able to tell the difference and act on it.

6\. Customer support

You own the standard for how customers are treated. That means knowing our response times to email, listening to how phone calls are actually handled, reading tickets, and spotting the patterns behind them. If refund requests spike, you should know why before anyone asks. If a VA is copy\-pasting canned replies that don't answer the question, you catch it and fix it.

What you'll build

Oversight keeps the business from breaking. The rest of the job is making it better.

Systems and workflows. We already have systems in place and they work — they're just simple. Your job is to take what exists and make it better, then document what isn't documented yet, so nothing depends on someone remembering.

Scorecards and KPIs. Every sector and every individual gets a scorecard. We already track creative team performance in Notion and Google Sheets — you'll extend that thinking across the whole business. The goal is that decisions about raises, warnings, and cuts become mechanical instead of emotional, and that nobody on payroll is quietly costing us money.

Automation. Find the repetitive work and get it out of human hands. There's a lot of it.

Hiring. When you find a gap, you fill it. You'll source, screen, and onboard.

Talent evaluation. Agencies and employees both. Are these the best people available to us at this price? If not, replace them. This is an ongoing job, not an annual review.

Staying current. E\-commerce moves fast. New AI tools, new services, new tactics that top brands are running. You should be finding these and bringing them in, not hearing about them from us six mont

Chief Development Officer \- (DEA00000510\)**Description**

Chief Development Officer Searches


Dedman College of Humanities and Sciences, Cox School of Business, and Dedman School of Law


Southern Methodist University


Dallas, Texas

  

THE SEARCHES


Southern Methodist University (SMU) seeks three accomplished, strategic, and collaborative advancement leaders to serve as the inaugural Chief Development Officers (CDOs) for the Dedman College of Humanities and Sciences, Cox School of Business, and the Dedman School of Law. These newly created positions represent a significant investment in the future of philanthropy at SMU and underscore the university’s commitment to building a best\-in\-class advancement enterprise capable of supporting its ambitious academic and institutional aspirations.


Southern Methodist University is experiencing a period of exceptional momentum. Under the leadership of President Jay Hartzell and Senior Vice President for Development and External Affairs Shontel Grumhaus, the university is reimagining its advancement model and investing in the people, processes, and infrastructure needed to elevate fundraising performance across the institution. The creation of these three executive\-level positions marks the first phase of that transformation and reflects a commitment to building a more sophisticated, collaborative, and donor\-centered culture of philanthropy.


Reporting to the Vice President for Schools and Unit Development, Paula Voyles Jewell, and serving as a senior strategic partner to their respective dean, each CDO will lead the development strategy for a major academic unit while helping shape the future of advancement at SMU. These leaders will have the opportunity to establish new standards for donor engagement, stewardship, prospect strategy, and team development while working alongside deans who are deeply committed to philanthropy and eager to expand their external engagement efforts.


The opportunities across these three academic units are substantial. The Dedman College of Humanities and Sciences, the university’s largest and most academically diverse academic unit, presents extensive opportunities to deepen donor engagement across its 16 departments and nine interdisciplinary institutes and centers. Following an extensive renovation and expansion project, the Cox School of Business is building on strong donor engagement and recent fundraising success to support ambitious priorities in faculty excellence, entrepreneurship, technology, experiential learning, and business innovation. Similarly, the Dedman School of Law is advancing a transformative capital initiative for a new law school facility on the university’s growing East Campus while cultivating a highly accomplished alumni base with significant philanthropic capacity.


As inaugural leaders in these roles, the CDOs will inherit exceptional philanthropic potential. SMU boasts visionary institutional and advancement leadership, a deeply loyal alumni community, influential volunteer leaders, and access to one of the country’s most dynamic metropolitan regions. University leadership believes the institution possesses extraordinary untapped fundraising opportunity and is thereby making a deliberate investment to realize that potential.


The successful candidates will be accomplished fundraisers and collaborative leaders who bring strategic vision, intellectual curiosity, and a record of building strong partnerships across complex organizations. They will be energized by the opportunity to help shape a growing advancement enterprise, serve as trusted advisors to academic leadership, and play defining roles in the next chapter of philanthropic success at Southern Methodist University.


Southern Methodist University has retained Jack Gorman of the national executive search firm Isaacson, Miller to conduct these important recruitments. Confidential inquiries, nominations, and applications may be directed to the search firm as indicated at the end of this posting.


ABOUT Southern Methodist University


A nationally ranked private university located near the heart of Dallas, Southern Methodist University is a distinguished center for global research and teaching. SMU’s more than 12,000 diverse, high\-achieving students come from all 50 states and over 80 countries to take advantage of the university’s small classes, meaningful research opportunities, leadership development, community service, international study, and innovative programs.


The university serves approximately 7,000 undergraduates and 5,000 graduate students through eight degree\-granting schools: Dedman College of Humanities and Sciences, Cox School of Business, Lyle School of Engineering, Meadows School of the Arts, Simmons School of Education and Human Development, Dedman School of Law, Perkins School of Theology, and Mood School of Graduate and Advanced Studies. SMU is data driven, and its powerful supercomputing ecosystem – paired with entrepreneurial drive – creates an unrivaled environment for the university to deliver research excellence.


Now in its second century of achievement, SMU is recognized for the ways it supports students, faculty, and alumni as they become ethical, enterprising leaders in their professions and communities. SMU’s relationship with Dallas – the dynamic center of one of the nation’s fastest\-growing regions – offers learning, research, social, and career opportunities that provide a launch pad for global impact.


Fundraising and Financial Overview


The Office of Development and External Affairs (DEA) comprises 147 professionals and supports Southern Methodist University by securing funding for university priorities; promoting meaningful involvement in the life and work of the university; heightening international, national, state, and local awareness of SMU; and supporting the enrollment of a diverse and able student body. In Fiscal Year 2026, SMU raised over $300 million
